definitions.explanation: a high flame or heat setting used in cooking, typically for quick searing or stir-frying

examples.japanese: {強火|つよび}で{一気|いっき}に{焼|や}く。
{強火|つよび}で{炒|いた}めると{香|かお}りが{出|で}る。
examples.english: Stir-frying on high heat brings out the aroma.

examples.japanese: チャーハンは{強火|つよび}で{作|つく}るのが{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: The basic rule is to make fried rice on high heat.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}は{強火|つよび}で{沸騰|ふっとう}させる。
examples.english: First, bring to a boil on high heat.

examples.japanese: {強火|つよび}で{表面|ひょうめん}をカリッと{焼|や}く。
examples.english: Sear the surface to make it crispy on high heat.

notes:
HEAT LEVELS IN COOKING:
- {弱火|よわび} (low heat)
- {中火|ちゅうび} (medium heat)
- {強火|つよび} (high heat)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {強火|つよび}で{焼|や}く (to sear on high heat)
- {強火|つよび}で{炒|いた}める (to stir-fry on high heat)
- {強火|つよび}で{沸|わ}かす (to boil on high heat)

COOKING TIPS:
{強火|つよび} is essential for:
- {中華料理|ちゅうかりょうり} (Chinese cooking) - wok cooking
- チャーハン (fried rice)
- ステーキ (steak) - initial sear
- {野菜炒|やさいいた}め (stir-fried vegetables)
